title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Purpose
-------
This playbook documents Redwood Inference's standardized hiring process, employee onboarding checklist, performance and feedback cycles, and practical guidance for managers. The goal is consistent candidate experience, fast and fair time-to-hire, predictable new hire ramp, and transparent performance practices across teams.

Scope
-----
Applies to all hiring and people manager activities at Redwood Inference for full-time employees (FTEs), contractors (where relevant), and internal transfers. Exceptions (e.g., executive hires, legal-sensitive roles) must be handled with People Ops and Legal.

Ownership and SLA
-----------------
- Owner: People Ops (primary), Hiring Manager (secondary).
- Time-to-fill target: 45 calendar days for IC roles, 60 days for manager roles.
- Time-to-offer target: 10 business days from final interview.
- New-hire first-week readiness: 100% of equipment and access provisioned by Day 1.

1) Hiring process (standard)
---------------------------
Overview: People Ops partners with hiring managers to create a repeatable, low-bias hiring workflow. Steps below are required unless an exception is documented and approved.

1. Requisition and Role Definition (Owner: Hiring Manager + People Ops)
   - Draft/approve job description using the JD template. Include: mission, top outcomes (3), required vs. preferred skills, expected level and IC/manager definition.
   - Define interview loop (roles and rubric owners) and expected interview duration.
   - Determine compensation band (People Ops provides band lookup).

2. Sourcing and Screening (Owner: Hiring Manager/Recruiter)
   - Sourcing channels: internal referrals (priority), LinkedIn, GitHub (for engineering), partner universities, targeted communities.
   - Initial screen (30 min): values, alignment, and basic skills. Use screening checklist.
   - For internal candidates, run a short calibration conversation with their manager and People Ops.

3. Interview Loop and Evaluation (Owner: Interviewers + Hiring Manager)
   - Structure: take-home challenge (when applicable) -> technical/role interview(s) -> cross-functional interview -> manager interview -> final panel.
   - Use the standardized scorecard for each interview. Interviewers must submit scorecards within 48 hours.
   - Scorecard rubric quick reference:

   | Category            | 0-4 score meaning           | Example criteria                 |
   |---------------------|-----------------------------|----------------------------------|
   | Role Skills         | 0: No evidence; 4: Excellent| problem-solving, stack knowledge |
   | Product & Impact    | 0-4                         | craft tradeoffs, customer focus  |
   | Communication       | 0-4                         | clarity, collaboration           |
   | Culture & Values    | 0-4                         | ownership, inclusive behavior    |

4. Decision and Offer (Owner: Hiring Manager + People Ops)
   - Hiring managers collate scorecards and write a 1-paragraph decision rationale.
   - People Ops runs compensation check and prepares an offer packet (base, equity, sign-on if approved, benefits).
   - Offer timeline: aim to extend verbal offer within 2 business days of decision.
   - If declined, capture candidate feedback in the ATS.

5. Background Checks and Closing (Owner: People Ops)
   - Initiate background check and reference checks (role-dependent).
   - Upon passing checks, confirm start date and begin pre-boarding.

Candidate experience best practices
- Communicate next steps after every interview milestone.
- Provide interview feedback when candidates request it.
- Keep interview loops lean: no more than 6 interviewers across the loop for non-exec roles.

2) Pre-boarding and Equipment provisioning
----------------------------------------
Timeline and owners:
- 14 days before start: People Ops sends welcome email with first-week schedule, paperwork links, access checklist, and manager onboarding plan.
- 7 days before start: IT/Laptop provisioning team confirms order and estimated delivery.
- 3 days before start: Manager shares team agenda and first-week projects.

Pre-boarding checklist (must be completed before Day 1):
- Signed offer and completed tax/HR forms.
- Laptop order placed and courier arranged.
- Corporate accounts requested (email, Slack, internal tools).
- Security awareness training invite sent.

3) Day 1 and First Week onboarding
----------------------------------
Day 1 (Owner: Manager + Buddy):
- Welcome meeting (30 min) with People Ops for high-level orientation.
- Manager 1:1 (60 min) covering role expectations, 30/60/90 goals, communication norms.
- Team lunch (in-person or virtual) and buddy introduction.
- Access verification and essential tool walkthrough.

First-week priorities:
- Complete mandatory compliance training (security, privacy, code of conduct).
- Small first-week project to ship (documentation update, small bugfix, or data review) to ensure early impact.
- Schedule recurring 1:1 cadence with manager (weekly for first 90 days).

First 30/60/90 day plan (template for managers):
- 30-day outcomes: Understand core systems, meet key partners, deliver first small project.
- 60-day outcomes: Ship improvements, own a small product or infra area, provide feedback on onboarding.
- 90-day outcomes: Fully ramped on primary responsibilities and present a 90-day review with manager.

4) Performance and feedback cycles
--------------------------------
Annual cycle (high-level)
- Quarterly check-ins: informal 1:1-based checkpoints to discuss goals, blockers, and growth.
- Mid-year review: written self-assessment and manager assessment; calibration across teams.
- Year-end review: final rating, merit increase recommendations, and calibration panel.

Objectives and goal-setting
- Managers and ICs co-create goals using OKR-style outcomes: 3 top priorities per quarter with measurable success criteria.
- Goals should map to team OKRs and be specific, measurable and time-bound.

Feedback best practices for managers
- Provide frequent, specific, and actionable feedback. Use the 5:1 ratio guidance (5 pieces of positive/strength feedback for every corrective note).
- Document coaching conversations in one-line notes (private to manager) and follow-up actions.
- Encourage peer feedback and incorporate cross-functional insights in performance summaries.

Calibration and ratings
- Calibration panels occur after manager reviews and before compensation recommendations.
- Calibration focuses on impact, consistency, and scope; avoid comparing different levels directly.
- Rating bands: Exceeds Expectations, Meets Expectations, Needs Improvement.

Performance improvement and PIP
- For persistent performance gaps, managers should:
  1. Create a documented performance plan with clear outcomes, timelines (typically 60-90 days), and support resources.
  2. Work with People Ops to ensure fairness and access to coaching.
  3. Escalate to Director+ and Legal if termination is being considered.

5) Manager-specific guidance and checklist
-----------------------------------------
On hiring:
- Build balanced interview panels with diverse perspectives.
- Ensure each interviewer has a clear rubric and question set.
- Debrief within 48 hours and capture decision rationale.

On onboarding:
- Send a 30/60/90 plan on Day 1.
- Schedule weekly 1:1s for the first 90 days and reduce cadence only after explicit agreement.
- Assign a buddy and clarify expectations for knowledge transfer.

On development and retention:
- Create individual development plans (IDPs) during the first 60 days.
- Identify stretch assignments and mentor matches.
- Discuss career pathways and promotion criteria openly.

On offboarding and exit interviews:
- Initiate knowledge transfer checklist 30 days prior to planned offboarding.
- Conduct an exit interview (People Ops lead) and capture reasons, themes, and actionable items.

6) Templates and artifacts (location pointers)
---------------------------------------------
- Job description template: /confluence/templates/jd-template
- Interview scorecard: /confluence/templates/interview-scorecard
- Offer letter templates: /confluence/templates/offer-letters
- 30/60/90 template: /confluence/templates/30-60-90
- New hire checklist (CSV): /confluence/people-ops/new-hire-checklist.csv

7) Metrics and continuous improvement
------------------------------------
Key metrics (tracked in People Ops dashboard):
- Time-to-fill (median)
- Time-to-offer
- Offer acceptance rate
- First-90-day retention
- Hiring source performance (referrals vs. external)
- New-hire ramp time (time to full productivity)

Continuous improvement rituals
- Quarterly hiring retrospective with recruiters and hiring managers to review dropped candidates, bias incidents, and interview quality.
- Onboarding NPS survey at Day 7 and Day 90; target Day 7 NPS > 60.

FAQ and common scenarios
------------------------
Q: What if a candidate requests flexible start date?
A: Consult People Ops; reasonable accommodations are encouraged and may shift equipment timelines.

Q: How do we handle internal transfers where the employee's current manager objects?
A: People Ops will mediate; prioritize career growth while respecting business needs and notice periods.

Q: Who signs off on compensation exceptions?
A: Director of People Ops (for >5% deviation) and CFO for material exceptions.

Glossary and Definitions
------------------------
- Time-to-fill: days between requisition approval and accepted offer.
- Ramp: time until employee reaches expected baseline productivity for role level.

Appendices
---------
Appendix A: Sample Interviewer Scorecard Questions
- Tell me about a time you delivered a feature under a tight deadline. What tradeoffs did you make?
- For engineers: review a small code sample (5-15 lines) and ask about complexity and edge cases.
- For product roles: discuss a product decision you influenced with metrics.

Appendix B: Example 30/60/90 Template
- 30 days: Learn systems, meet stakeholders, complete first task.
- 60 days: Own a component, propose improvements.
- 90 days: Deliver a scoped initiative and present outcomes.

If you have suggested edits or edge cases to add, please open a PR on the People Ops handbook repo or contact People Ops (people-ops@redwood-inference.com).
